summary: Mathematical dossier for THE SHAPE AND ITS SHADOW: a 170-second, seven-act film separating exact geometry from the manuscript’s claimed all-dimensional theorem.
content:
Preserve the approved timing: 0–27, 27–49, 49–68, 68–82, 82–106, 106–150, 150–170 seconds. Captions replace one another; introduce symbols before assembling formulas. Mathematical coordinates remain distinct from display offsets.

1. Polarity from constraints

A convex body K⊂Rⁿ is compact, convex, and has nonempty interior. Require K=−K; consequently 0∈int K. Define K°={y: x·y≤1 for every x∈K}, and P(K)=|K||K°|, where bars denote n-dimensional Lebesgue volume. “Shadow” is a metaphor, not an optical projection.

For K=[−1,1]³, maximizing independently in each coordinate gives maxₓ∈K x·y=|y₁|+|y₂|+|y₃|. Thus K°={y: Σ|yᵢ|≤1}. Necessity follows by choosing xᵢ=sign(yᵢ); sufficiency follows from xᵢyᵢ≤|yᵢ|.

A nonzero boundary point y defines a supporting plane x·y=1. Interior polar points define non-touching bounding planes; exterior points violate a cube constraint. Begin with y=e₁, touching a square face; y=(1/2,1/3,1/6) touches (1,1,1). Implement a plane patch as y/‖y‖²+up+vq, with orthonormal p,q perpendicular to y and bounded u,v. Explain x, y, dot product, and threshold before naming polarity.

Cube geometry: eight vertices (±1,±1,±1), six square faces, twelve edges. Octahedron: six vertices ±eᵢ; its eight triangular faces are conv(s₁e₁,s₂e₂,s₃e₃), one per sign triple. Both solids are topological closed 3-balls; their boundaries are spheres, not tori.

2. Exact dissection and sections

Each solid tetrahedron Q_s=conv(0,s₁e₁,s₂e₂,s₃e₃) has four triangular faces. Its points are Σrᵢsᵢeᵢ with rᵢ≥0 and Σrᵢ≤1. Each outer triangle can be parametrized by (1−u−v)s₁e₁+us₂e₂+vs₃e₃, u,v≥0, u+v≤1. Use explicit triangles, not a rectangular parameter domain spilling beyond the face.

The eight tetrahedra have disjoint interiors and tile K°. Base conv(0,s₁e₁,s₂e₂) has area 1/2; perpendicular height is 1. Therefore |Q_s|=(1/3)(1/2)(1)=1/6, |K°|=8/6=4/3, |K|=2³=8, and P(K)=32/3=4³/3!.

For z=h, |h|≤1, the octahedron section is |x|+|y|≤1−|h|: vertices (±(1−|h|),0,h), (0,±(1−|h|),h), area 2(1−|h|)². Its integral over h is 4/3. Cube sections have area 4. Exploded tetrahedra are displaced copies; restore them before asserting containment.

3. Reciprocal deformation

For invertible T, y∈(TK)° iff Tᵀy∈K°, hence (TK)°=T⁻ᵀK°. Determinant factors cancel: |TK|=|det T||K| and |T⁻ᵀK°|=|det T|⁻¹|K°|.

Use T_τ=diag(2^τ,(3/2)^τ,(1/2)^τ), 0≤τ≤1. Update every polar point with the reciprocal diagonal at the same τ. Then (T_τx)·(T_τ⁻ᵀy)=x·y throughout motion. At τ=1, det T=3/2, volumes are 12 and 8/9, and product remains 32/3. Independent linear vertex interpolations generally break polarity between endpoints.

4. Round comparison

For the unit ball B, maxₓ∈B x·y=‖y‖₂, so B°=B. Cauchy–Schwarz supplies the upper bound; x=y/‖y‖ attains it for y≠0. Use sphere parametrization (sinφ cosθ,sinφ sinθ,cosφ), φ∈[0,π], θ∈[0,2π]. Horizontal sections have radius √(1−h²). Volume is 4π/3; product is 16π²/9≈17.545963, exceeding 32/3≈10.666667. Their ratio is π²/6≈1.644934.

5. Attributed theorem and analytic lens

With the origin-symmetric convex-body hypothesis visible, attribute P(K)≥4ⁿ/n!, n≥1, and the Hanner equality classification to the supplied manuscript. The general symmetric 3D theorem predates it: [Iriyeh–Shibata](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01749). Computing one cube does not prove that theorem.

The supplied notes specify D={v+it: |t|≤1, |v|≤λ(t)}, with λ even, positive inside, λ(±1)=0, and λ″(t)=−sec(πt/2). The conformal map onto int D is F(z)=(8/π²)Σⱼ≥₀(−1)ʲz²ʲ⁺¹/(2j+1)². Implementable width: λ(t)=Re F(exp(iπt/2)). A tilted planar embedding is c+vp+tq, with p=(1,0,0), q=(0,cosβ,sinβ), β=π/5. Fill using v=rλ(t), r∈[−1,1]. D is a topological disk.

Label this “schematic of the analytic input,” including when numerically sampled. Never substitute an unlabeled ellipse. Uniform boundary angle produces ελ(T)+iT, with T uniform on [−1,1] and independent fair sign ε. This sampling law and the holomorphic mass estimate are inputs, not visually proved facts.

6. Feasible simplices and integrated volume

Use A={X: |bᵢ·X|≤1}; rows bᵢ are nonzero, pairwise nonproportional, and span Rⁿ. Then A°=conv{±bᵢ}. For X∈int A, set L_X={Y: |bᵢ·Y|≤λ(bᵢ·X)}.

Choose an unordered independent n-row subset I and signs εᵢ. Solve bᵢ·Y=εᵢλ(bᵢ·X), i∈I. It is feasible precisely when the solution satisfies every remaining constraint. Its simplex is conv(0,{εᵢbᵢ:i∈I}); volume is |det B_I|/n!. Define Σ_X as their union. Each simplex lies in A° by convexity. The manuscript asserts their interiors are disjoint almost everywhere; general unions may leave gaps.

Explain P_I as the feasibility probability: sample independent uniform Tᵢ and fair εᵢ, solve B_IX=T and B_IY=ελ(T), and require X∈A and Y∈L_X. I indexes row subsets, not eight separately counted cube orthants. Change of variables gives P_I=|det B_I|4⁻ⁿ∫_AΣ_ε1_feasible dX.

Reveal 1≤S=Σ_I P_I=(n!/4ⁿ)∫_A|Σ_X|dX≤(n!/4ⁿ)|A||A°|. Explain n!, normalization, integration over X, simplex volume, and containment separately. The first inequality is the manuscript’s analytic input; the equality uses sampling, determinants, and almost-everywhere disjointness; the last inequality uses containment. Approximation extends the polytope statement.

For the cube, bᵢ=eᵢ and Yᵢ=εᵢλ(Xᵢ): all eight signs are feasible for every interior X. Thus Σ_X=K°, the integral is 32/3, and S=(6/64)(32/3)=1. Moving X must not create missing-volume dynamics in this example.

7. Equality’s family

Hanner bodies start from centered intervals. In complementary coordinate spaces form H₁×H₂ or conv((H₁,0)∪(0,H₂)); polarity exchanges these operations. A mixed 3D example is the square bipyramid conv((±1,±1,0),(0,0,±1)); its polar is {|x|+|y|≤1, |z|≤1}. Their volumes are 8/3 and 4, again giving 32/3. This illustrates recursion; it does not establish the classification.

Closing card: “OpenAI manuscript — September 22, 2026 — family 087. Formalization reported by the source; not independently checked for this film.” The [pinned scope page](https://github.com/HarleyCoops/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/lean/docs/087.md) reports the symmetric theorem and equality classification.
